one_liner: Take a melody people already love, move it into an unexpected genre and another decade, on a channel that only makes that sound.
formula_html: Take a melody people already love, move it into an unexpected genre and another decade, on a channel that only makes that sound.
start_here: Choose one sound for the channel and name it after that sound (Channel → name).
Set up the channel and the upload settings once (Channel).
Make idea #1 with the Spanish long-video recipe, then cut its chorus into a Short.
Run its two thumbnails through YouTube Studio's Test & Compare.
Fill the scorecard at day 7 and day 28; keep what lands in its band.

tracks.label: Spanish · long video
tracks.summary: 12 outliers vs 12 ordinary videos of the same channels. The older videos had no pattern to test, so treat this as strong evidence, not proof.

arrangement.title: Content formula — a genre-swap cover, about 4:30
arrangement.caption: Coloured blocks: what to put where. Amber frame: where viewers rewind most.

cards.title: Title
cards.example: Tradicional mexicana – La Llorona | Cover IA Heavy Metal 80s dramático
do: Name the new genre and the decade
One emotion word: emotivo, dramático, épico
dont: Name a real singer whose voice you imitate
Leave out the genre — it is the promise

evidence.label: The concept behind it
evidence.concept: genre-swap cover of a famous song

cards.title: Thumbnail
cards.template:
Photoreal performer styled in the NEW genre, face visible
Big text: [CANCIÓN] / Versión [Género]
Small corner text: Generado con IA
cards.example: A rock singer in a white rebozo with an electric guitar, rain and candles — “LA LLORONA / Versión Heavy Metal”
do: Text = song + genre, or no text when the era scene says it
dont: Make the singer look like a real artist

cards.title: Sound & picture
cards.template:
Master around −16 LUFS, keep the dynamics
One cinematic scene or a slow push-in — cuts optional
4–6 min for one song · 25–30 min for a mix

cards.title: Description
cards.template:
[Género] [época] con [instrumentos]: “[Canción]” reimaginada [emoción].

[2–3 líneas: la historia de la canción y de esta versión]

🎶 Arreglo y voz creados con IA · melodía tradicional / de dominio público.
🔔 Suscríbete: [tu promesa, p. ej. un clásico en heavy metal cada viernes]

#[género] #cover #coveria #[canción] #[época] #musicaconia #[emoción] #[canal]
cards.example: Heavy metal de los 80 con guitarras gemelas y doble bombo: “La Llorona” reimaginada con todo su drama.
do: First line = the style in plain words
Say it is made with AI
dont: Paste someone else's prompt or lyrics

cards.title: Edit

0:00 sing the hook — no intro
0:02 first picture change, then every ~7 s
Lyric captions, the sung word highlighted
End on the first frame so it loops · 15–60 s, vertical

channel.title: Channel name
channel.template: [the sound] + [a craft, place or era word] — 2–3 words, in your audience's language

dont: “AI” in the name — say it in the description instead

channel.template:
@[NameWithoutSpaces] (20 characters or fewer)

About:
[What, in one line: “Canciones tradicionales en heavy metal de los 80.”]
[When: “Un clásico nuevo cada viernes.”]
[How: “Arreglos y voces creados con IA; melodías tradicionales o de dominio público.”]

channel.title: Series & playlists
channel.template:
One repeated signature on every title: “| Cover IA Heavy Metal emotivo”, “(Flamenco 2026)”
One playlist per series · end screen → the next song of the series

evidence.label: Signatures
evidence.text: see “repeated signature” in the channel table below

channel.title: Upload rhythm
channel.template:
1–2 long videos a week, on fixed days
+ a Short trailer for each long video

channel.title: Pinned comment
channel.template:
Pin your own first comment: where to go next —
the next song of the series, another version of this song, or the playlist
channel.example: “¿Te gusta el soul? Escucha La Paloma en Bolero Soul 1955 → [link]”

evidence.label: On the outliers
evidence.text: 7 of the 25 outliers whose comments were read had the creator's comment on top (sequel, other version, community)

channel.title: Upload settings (every video)
channel.template:
Category: Music
Video & title language: Spanish / English
Comments: on
Audience: not made for kids
Altered or synthetic content: yes, when it looks or sounds real
Subtitles: upload the lyrics (Shorts: burn them in)
Visibility: public, at your fixed day and hour
dont: Mark it “made for kids” (it turns comments off)

evidence.label: Disclosure, audience, category
evidence.text: not visible in the data — YouTube policy and good practice; the category made no measurable difference

ideas_lead: Score = evidence × demand × gap (each 1 to 3, from the concept table) − cost. Predicted band = the result to expect against your own channel's median. Every melody is traditional, public domain, or yours.

confidence: English long videos: the patterns held in the back-test (median 2.14× vs 1.43× on newer videos).
Spanish long videos: strong patterns, but the older half had none to test against.
Shorts: few outliers, and the patterns failed the back-test — observations only.
Every view count re-checked on YouTube's watch pages matched (12 of 12).
Known flaw, fixed for the next run: this run's controls were not checked for the niche, so “the title names the AI” is not a finding.
Concept outlier rates look high because search results lean to videos that already did well — compare the lift.
Vision labels: thumbnails 72/72 (spot-checked); opening frames only 3/50 (shared CPU) — the frames were reviewed by eye.
risks: Covers of copyrighted songs get Content ID claims: the money goes to the rights holder. Use traditional / public-domain melodies (old melody and words, not a modern arrangement) or your own songs.
Imitating a real singer's voice or face breaks YouTube's rules and, in places, the law.
YouTube asks you to disclose realistic AI content, and it does not monetise mass-produced, repetitive (“inauthentic”) content — vary the songs and make real choices in each one.
Free tiers of hosted AI music tools are usually non-commercial — check the terms before monetising.
Tutorials and AI-music news are crowded and fading: only 2 of 21 new tutorials beat their channel's normal.
scorecard_text: For each published video, write its link and its views at 7 and 28 days, then divide by your channel's median (new channel: the median of your first 5 uploads). Keep what lands in or above its predicted band; drop what lands below twice.
